title: Which RNA samples are good enough to analyse?
prompt:
Create a large 16:9 landscape infographic for a general professional audience (managers, engineers new to the topic, students), light near-white background, warm and clear like a well-designed museum explainer or a quality newspaper graphic. Plain everyday language is the main text; technical names appear only as small grey secondary labels.

TITLE (large): "Which RNA samples are good enough to analyse?"
SUBTITLE: "How TOKN quality-checked six RNA-sequencing samples before any gene-expression results were drawn from them."

BAND 1 — heading "Why this matters": one wide card with a simple flat illustration of a sample tube beside a DNA-style sequencing read-out, and this text: "Gene-expression studies are only as good as their samples. A degraded or contaminated sample can create differences between groups that aren't really there."

BAND 2 — heading "Who did the work": a left-to-right flow of eight round role badges joined by arrows. Each badge shows a line icon, the bold role name, the short description in quotes, and the model name tiny and grey below:
1 Scout — "lists the tools available" (claude-haiku-5.5) [icon: binoculars]
2 Planner — "writes what 'done' looks like" (claude-opus-5.5) [icon: document]
3 Analyst — "runs the official checks" (Kimi-K3.1-Pro) [icon: bar chart]
4 Skeptic — "re-checks and finds 8 weak spots" (FW-GLM-5.3) [icon: shield]
5 Judge — "decides: revise or ship?" (Microsoft-Decision-1) [icon: balance scale]
6 Editor — "fixes every weak spot" (gpt-6.1-sol) [icon: pencil]
7 Coach — "writes a lesson for next time" (claude-opus-5.5) [icon: lightbulb]
8 Examiner — "scores it with plain code, no AI" (verify.py) [icon: checklist]
Caption under the flow: "Like a newsroom: a writer, a fact-checker, an editor — and an exam nobody can sweet-talk."

BAND 3 — heading "Four questions every sample must answer": four cards in a row, each with an icon, the question in large plain words, and a tiny grey tool label:
(RNA strand icon) "Is the RNA intact and every key measurement present?" — tiny grey label: assess_rnaseq_quality
(filter funnel icon) "Is it free of contamination and over-copying?" — tiny grey label: assess_rnaseq_quality
(side-by-side bars icon) "Does it look like the other samples?" — tiny grey label: compare_samples
(two overlapping circles icon) "Can lab batch and study group still be told apart?" — tiny grey label: check_batch_confound

BAND 4 — heading "What it found": 6 result cards in a row. Each shows the small ID at top, a large verdict word in its color with a matching status icon, and one plain sentence:
S01 — green (#16A34A) verdict "Include" — "Every quality measure passes."
S02 — green (#16A34A) verdict "Include, just" — "RNA integrity 7.0 and mapping 80% sit exactly on the pass line."
S03 — red (#DC2626) verdict "Exclude" — "RNA integrity 5.9 is below the hard limit of 6."
S04 — amber (#D97706) verdict "Flag for review" — "34% duplicate reads: usable with caution."
S05 — purple (#7C3AED) verdict "Can't certify" — "RNA integrity was never measured; nothing is assumed."
S06 — red (#DC2626) verdict "Exclude" — "22.4% ribosomal RNA: the library preparation likely failed."
Small note at the right of the heading: "A missing measurement is never filled in with a guess."

BOTTOM BAND — three short panels:
"Trust, but verify" — "An independent checker re-ran the checks and plain code graded the result: 6 of 6 correct."
"Honest wording" — "'Include' means fit for analysis, not proof of a biological effect."
"Getting better each run" — "The lesson saved for next time: Copy every gate status word for word; never relabel it."

FOOTER (small, centered): "The takeaway: A sample you can't measure is a sample you can't trust."

TEXT DISCIPLINE: use ONLY the words given above in quotes plus the headings. Do NOT add any slogans, taglines, mottos, handwritten notes, brand lines, decorative words, extra footers or invented statistics. Every word spelled exactly as given and legible at 4K.

Visual rules: generous whitespace, strong hierarchy (title > band headings > plain sentences > tiny grey technical labels), verdict colors only on the result cards, soft blue/teal section tints, flat friendly line icons. No people, no faces, no photos.
